title: NaviMed-UMB: hardware envelope studies for local AI deployment on consumer RDNA 4 GPUs

creators.name: Minarowski, Łukasz
creators.affiliation: Department of Respiratory Physiopathology, Medical University of Białystok, Poland

description:
NaviMed-UMB is an engineering log and reproducible benchmark suite for running modern open-weight large language models on a consumer-grade dual AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700 32 GB workstation (gfx1201, RDNA 4 / Navi 48) under ROCm 7.2 and vLLM 0.19. The repository is the L1 (engineering / hardware envelope) layer of a three-layer NaviMed program targeting sovereign on-premise medical AI for privacy-sensitive workloads.

The project provides: a reproducible benchmark protocol with explicit Phase 1 / Phase 2 gates and a strict §11 embargo classification; per-model software / hardware environment manifests; aggregated public engineering envelopes (§11.1) for a 21-model evaluation suite; an AWQ W4A16 release pipeline for the PLLuM family of Polish-language LLMs (8B Llama base, 12B Mistral-Nemo base, 70B Llama base; published as model cards on HuggingFace under mozarcik/; the 8B and 12B were quantised locally on the R9700 workstation, the 70B family on an AMD Instinct MI300X via the AMD Developer Cloud, powered by DigitalOcean, under the AMD Developer Program); a reusable Polish SmPC calibration corpus (mozarcik/clinical-pl-smpc-awq-calibration, 418 fragments of European Medicines Agency drug-information text, no patient health information). Version 0.5.0 adds Tier-A statistical re-runs (n = 10 per cell) of the Phase 2 suite, a same-checkpoint BF16↔AWQ precision-ablation sub-study (raw compute complete, aggregation in progress), an N = 1 single-stream latency anchor across all model families, a host-firmware (BIOS 1715→2202) reconciliation of the measurement provenance, and new public documentation of the Layer 2 retrieval architecture (hybrid BM25 + dense + reciprocal-rank fusion, a frozen measurement baseline, and an evidence-percolation direction).

Per-N throughput, latency and power-per-token figures are held under embargo (METHODOLOGY §11.2 / §11.3) pending peer-reviewed publication. Engineering envelopes, walltime, sanity-gate evidence and failure post-mortems are public (§11.1).

Intended audience: researchers preparing local AI infrastructure for privacy-sensitive workloads, hardware reviewers seeking reproducible RDNA 4 methodology, software maintainers working on RDNA 4 support in inference frameworks, and clinical-AI groups evaluating Polish-language LLMs.
notes: AI assistance disclosure: project documentation was prepared with assistance from large language models (Claude, Anthropic — models Opus 4.7 & 4.8 and Fable 5 [claude-fable-5], the latter for Claude Code subagent tasks; GPT, OpenAI; Gemini, Google; Bielik-11B-v3.0-instruct served locally via vLLM on the project's R9700 workstation for Polish-language editorial). All experimental design, hardware configuration, empirical measurements and scientific claims are the author's. AI tools did not execute experiments. See AI_USAGE_DISCLOSURE.md in the repository. Compute acknowledgement: the 70B AWQ family was quantised on an AMD Instinct MI300X (AMD Developer Cloud, powered by DigitalOcean) provided as a promotional credit under the AMD Developer Program; the 8B and 12B were quantised locally on the R9700 workstation. Base models are from the PLLuM consortium, published via CYFRAGOVPL (Polish Ministry of Digital Affairs).
